title: The Physician and the Paralytic
english: He brought their words as a gift, so that they might be justified by their words. For God, who knows the hearts, does not ignore what is said, but welcomed the word so that the question might draw out the energy. Thus the physician, having approached and having run to the one looking, asked this man: 'Do you want to be made well?' (and it is nothing to wonder if he had passed by the one lying beside the pool, if he had run from heaven to us), drawing him by the question into knowledge and stirring him up to inquiry. It was a gift of great grace, for he was unpaid. For this reason, he had the healer running to him.

As for the man toward him: 'Yes, Lord. For my long-standing sickness makes health desirable to me, but I have no man.' Do not be discouraged, man, because you have no man. You have God present, partly as man and partly as God; for both must be confessed. For the confession of humanity is not useful if the divinity is not co-confessed; rather, it is a curse to the one who brings it. For it is a curse to him who has hope in man. If we, even while hoping in Jesus, also hope in man without intertwining the divinity with our hope, we are heirs to a curse.

But now we confess both God and man, and both truly: God truly, having been born of the true Father, and man not according to a fantasy, but having been born according to truth; worshipping, we await true salvation. 'I want to be made well, but I have no man.' See, where salvation is lacking, there he gave the energy. For many of those suffering had houses, and even acquaintances, even if they had others. But this one, truly crushed in all poverty and having no power of external help, having been left most alone, had a helping son of God, the only-begotten.

'Do you want to be made well?' 'Yes, Lord, but I have no man, so that when the water is stirred, he might throw me into the pool.' You have the spring, for from you is the spring of life, a spring of spring-making.

But whoever drinks from this water, rivers will flow from within his belly, not water flowing downward, but water leaping (for Jesus does not make one leap from above to below, but from earthly things to the heavenly), water leaping into eternal life. For Jesus is the spring of good things. And why do you wait for a swimming pool? You have the one walking upon the waters, the one who rebukes the winds, the charioteer of the sea, the one who not only had the sea submit to him as a foundation of law, but also granted to Peter the similar energy of walking. For as soon as the night was without moon, the light was present, but it was not recognized (for Jesus walking upon the waters was unknown as far as his face appeared as a joy to a beast, but the uniqueness of his voice testified to the one present), and thinking he was a phantom, they were afraid. But Jesus said to them: 'I am, do not be afraid.' And Peter says to him: 'If it is you whom I know, but rather whom the Father testified to me, command me to come to you upon the waters.' And he who says to him with the most abundant transfer says: 'Come.'

Thus, beside the waters of the swimming pool, there was the charioteer and maker of the waters. To whom the paralytic says: 'I do not have a man, so that, when the water is troubled, he may throw me into the swimming pool.' The Savior says to him: 'Why do you wait for the troubling of waters? Unperturbed, be healed. And what apparent movement do you expect? By the word the command becomes sharper than thought. Only through the energy of the spring, fly above the one appearing in the flesh as God, and do not look at the one appearing, but at the one working through the one appearing. I do not have a man, so that when the water is troubled he may throw me into the swimming pool.' But he says to him: 'Why do you wait for small things? Why do you seek a healing of waters? Arise, the resurrection has said to you.' For everywhere to all people the Savior becomes all things: they hunger, he is bread; they thirst, he is water; to the dead, a resurrection; to the sick, a physician; to sinners, a redemption.

Arise, lift up your bed and walk. But first arise, first cast off the sickness. Then take up the cord of faith. First be strong against the one carrying your bed, and learn to carry the wooden vessel of long-revered things. And that one, the Savior, commanded to carry the wooden vessel, about which it is written: 'The king made a vessel for himself from the woods of Lebanon. He made its pillars silver, its canopy purple, and inside it was paved with stone.' The symbols of the passion are in the [...]

title: The Wisdom of the Songs
english: The songs lie near to bridal, sober, and well-minded things. For if one takes the words by considering the opinion of many and staring at nothing, he might think the songs are erotic and full of passion, but the words are bridal, filled with sobriety. And if you do not understand the songs by intellect, come to the proverbs, and ascend by way and by steps to those things. Wisdom built a house for herself (as the word is about a woman, Prov 9:1), and sent out her own servants. And again elsewhere it says: You have been loved by her and will keep her (Prov 2:17). It is not the love of a woman, but the love of wisdom defining its limits. For where there is the possession of wisdom, there is the definition of love. For passions are not according to wisdom, but thoughts are wise. Horses became female, the impulse being irrational. Therefore, if in the songs you hear what is said concerning a bridegroom and a bride, do not fall down, nor listen to these things passionably, but train the passions from the impassive ones.

Therefore, the divine study of the Songs, filled with sobriety, signifies the passion of Christ. For the things narrated concerning the passion of the Savior also mention the place: He entered into a garden, because of the one buried there. And he mentioned the aromas: He took my myrrh full; for the economy was fulfilled. And after the resurrection he said: I ate my bread with my honey (Rev 19:9). For they gave to him wax from the bee. And the songs again said things concerning the spikenard wine: I will make you drink from the fragrant wine. And regarding the ointment poured upon his head, elsewhere it says: Until the king reclines at his side, my nard gave his fragrance. For while he was reclining in the house of Simon the leper, a woman entered, having taken an alabaster jar of precious, faithful nard, and poured it upon his head (Mark 14:3). So also concerning the instrument of the cross. The wood of the cross, which carries, made its pillars silver. The beginning of the cross was silver, the betrayal. For just as a beautiful house has a golden roof lying above, while all the construction of it consists of pillars, so also the beginning of the crucifying and rising of Christ was silver. For if Judas had not handed him over, he would not have been crucified. Because of this, as naming the passion its beginning, it made its pillars silver.

His entry was into the purple. For this reason they clothed him in purple, playing indeed, but working prophetically; for he was a king. Even if they acted most according to mockery, they acted completely; and it became a symbol of royal dignity. And though it was a crown of thorns, it was a crown, and it was placed by soldiers. For kings are proclaimed by soldiers. His entry was into the purple, and within it was a paved floor. The diligent ones of the church know the paved floor, which is called Gabbatha, in the place where Pilate was.

These things have been written to me in a deviation regarding the one who came to the bed for the garment. He said therefore to him: 'Rise, take up your bed and walk.' The disease was for many years, but the plaster was sharp. The paralysis was for many years, but the cramp was sharp. For the Maker is the one providing various cures to the blind, the one who strangely granted the plaster through the application of mud. For to the one seeing, if mud is poured on him, it hinders seeing; but Jesus, through mud, granted seeing to those not seeing. And to others again, through other means, the power was shown; for to the one he said, 'Rise, take up your bed and walk.' How much astonishment do you think it took those seeing? But the thing seen was wonderful, while the unbelief was terrible. And a disease of many years is healed, but a long-standing unbelief was not healed. But the Jews persisted in their sufferings, and they did not want to be healed.

If it is necessary to be struck with amazement by what happens, it is necessary to worship the Physician of souls and bodies. But they were grumbling. For they were descendants of grumblers, those turning beautiful things into bad things, those saying the bitter is sweet, and the sweet is bitter. But Jesus was working with all economy on the Sabbath, working things concerning the Sabbath, so that the work might convince. Since word fights word, but the deed is unarguable, he healed on the Sabbath, teaching, so that the word might not become an adversarial word, but the work might convince those seeing.

They were arguing: 'It is a Sabbath, it is not permitted for you to carry your bed.' A lawgiver was present, and another was saying 'it is not permitted for you.' 'Establish, Lord, a lawgiver over them,' as it has been said concerning the Savior. But he, having been fully healed both soul and body by the Physician, having received a wise word from Wisdom, immediately...

title: The Power of the Word
english: He answers, not having the sense of a legalistic reply, but making his answer brief. Listen to me, he says, all of you, to the long-standing disease and the many-year reclining, the boundless misery. None of you ever showed care by taking me and first putting me into the bath so that I might be healed. Even if then you did not show care, how now you have received the legislative command, saying, 'Is it not permitted to you to take your bed?' Therefore I make my answer to you most brief: he who made me well said this to me. If you despise me, take astonishment at the matter. He did not apply plaster, he did not use medical machines or aids. He spoke a word, and the work followed. He commanded, and I fulfill the command. I have become obedient to this, to the command of him who healed through commands. For if the one who commanded was powerless in his commands, it would not have been necessary to obey these. Since he has commanded in clear words to stop a long-standing suffering, I hear this most justly, he of whom even the disease, having heard, was healed. He who made me well said to me, 'Pick up your bed' (Mark 2:11).
16 The one healed did not know who the healer was. Much of the unostentatious nature of our Savior is presented. For having healed, he departed,

so that he might not be made known through the healing. But we do the exact opposite. If it ever happens to us to behold visions, or to help through the hands, or to drive away a demon by calling upon [him], we refrain so much from hiding the miracle that even without being asked, we boast. But Jesus, teaching us through his works not to speak about himself, while providing the healing, deviated at once so that he might not be known, withdrawing at an opportune time and being present at an opportune time. For when it was necessary for the fame of the miracle to be shut up, then he withdraws. But when the departure of the crowds had happened, so that he might lead them after the bodily healing to the things of the soul having been healed, then being present he said: 'See, you have become well; sin no more.'

For the physician is varied, sometimes first healing the soul and then the body, and sometimes conversely. 'Sin no more, so that nothing may happen to you.' He teaches many through one. For the word is not toward that [one] alone, but indeed toward all of us. For if ever we fall into sufferings or sorrows or necessities, let no one write [it] down to God. For God is infinite of evils, but he himself tests no one. But each of us, being squeezed by rows of sins, is flogged. 'Sin no more, so that nothing may happen to you.' Let every man hear the spoken word, and let him who is committing fornication before this cast off the passion, and he who before...

Let the greedy man become merciful. Let the paralytic hear: sin no more. God's forgetfulness of sin is great, and His grace is abundant. But do not take the excess of His forbearance as an excuse for contempt, nor sin because God is long-suffering.

Rather, be healed of fleshly passions, and you also speak of what was read at the opportune time. For when we were in the flesh, the sufferings of sins were working through the law in our members; but when the apostle says, 'when we were in the flesh' (Romans 8:9), he was not speaking of this flesh which we are clothed in, but of fleshly deeds. He still said 'flesh' while wearing flesh, when he said 'when we were in the flesh.' But regarding the manner in which the flood was about to come, God said, 'My spirit shall not abide in these men, because they are flesh' (Genesis 6:3), because they were changing from the Spirit into a fleshly will; in this same way, here the apostle says, 'when we were in the flesh.'

Therefore, let no one be in the flesh (2 Corinthians 5:7), but being in the flesh, let him not walk according to the flesh (Galatians 5:16). For the apostle does not want us, having brought ourselves completely out of the world, to do no evil, but rather, being in the flesh, to enslave the flesh and not be ruled by it. Let us not be enslaved, but let us rule. Let us use food in moderation, not being carried away by gluttony, but bridling [it].

[...regarding] the stomach, so that we may also begin from those things under the stomach. Let the body be ruled by the soul, and let not the soul be dragged under the fleshly pleasures. Sin no more, so that nothing worse may happen to you. Indeed the word preaches to all, but let all ears be capable of hearing. For not every hearing of the flesh that receives the word already receives it into the mind. Because of this the Savior was saying: 'Let the one having ears to hear, hear' (Matt 13:9), while conversing with those having ears of the flesh. Let everyone then hear Jesus and sin no more (John 8:11), but let us run to the one who forgives the transgressions. And if we are sick, let us flee to him; whether we are suffering...
